critical_findings.finding: The native baseline already uses all 1460 event slots. Any IR-v2 implementation that adds compiler-source events can overflow before the new representation is qualified.
The native baseline uses all 64 parameter slots. Adding helper functions with parameters can overflow the current parameter capacity. Prefer in-place lowering or measured bounded capacity expansion.
Only 10 measured call-argument slots remain. New helper-call-heavy code is unsafe without remeasurement and a bounded pool update.
Only 74 call records remain at the native baseline. Avoid unnecessary helper calls during the structural IR-v2 patch.

compaction_candidate.rule: Do not serialize the aggregate discard-keyword event into the codegen/event stream when the actual side-effecting call/store remains represented independently.
safety_constraints: Never drop a call because its result is discarded.
Never drop a store because its result is discarded.
Never infer side effects from source text in the emitter.
The builder must retain the real side-effecting instruction and only remove the redundant aggregate discard marker.
The projected 761 count is not a PASS until measured by the real Stage1 path on Linux x86-64.

requirements: Preserve the closed 736/746 call-argument evidence as the historical baseline.
Prefer removing redundant structural events over adding large speculative banks.
Add bounded storage only if the compacted native source still requires it.
Avoid new helper functions with parameters while parameter capacity remains exactly full.
Avoid unnecessary helper calls while call/call-argument headroom remains low.
Run focused non-native tests before Linux qualification.
Remeasure every changed count on native Linux x86-64 before declaring the capacity checkpoint PASS.
Do not start the general emitter, SELF_EMIT, or Stage2 until IR-v2 construction and verification pass.
